what_this_is: Ongoing scan of the niche selected by CONTENT TYPE and format only (Shorts <=90s matching eight topic-type queries), no channel-size filter. Provides two separate things: a global view anchor, and a size-controlled per-category signal used for topic selection.

prior_basis.statistic: median views of Shorts from channels under 1,000 subscribers
prior_basis.why_not_the_unfiltered_pool: median of the full unfiltered pool is 1,457,914 views, 1,400x this channel's reality. An unfiltered pool cannot yield a usable absolute number without some size conditioning, so a size band is used for THIS number only. The category signal below uses the full unfiltered pool.

category_signal_notes: Residuals are measured against same-size peers, so they carry content-type signal with channel size divided out. Raw per-category view medians are NOT usable - they track the size mix of whichever channels the query surfaced (median subs per category ranged 1,860 to 988,500). These multipliers are for TOPIC SELECTION only and never multiply a predicted view count: between-category spread (0.93 log10) is about the same as within-category spread (0.97 log10), so they rank topic types but cannot forecast an individual video.

category_provenance.method: per-category mean of log10(views) residuals against a least-squares fit on log10(subscribers); multiplier = 10^mean_residual, where 1.0 is par for a channel that size
